title: Diagnostic Likelihood Ratios: From Pretest to Posttest Probability
subject: PSM
preview: Sensitivity and specificity describe test characteristics; likelihood ratios link test results to pretest probability.
quickRevision: Sensitivity and specificity describe test characteristics; likelihood ratios link test results to pretest probability.
Likelihood ratios are not themselves the posttest probability; odds-based updating is required.
Spectrum effects and test thresholds can change real-world test performance.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: Sensitivity and specificity describe test characteristics; likelihood ratios link test results to pretest probability.
A positive likelihood ratio greater than one tends to increase probability, while a negative ratio below one tends to decrease it.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: Likelihood ratios are not themselves the posttest probability; odds-based updating is required.
Spectrum effects and test thresholds can change real-world test performance.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not interpret an isolated test result without an estimate of prior clinical probability.

quiz.question: What does a negative likelihood ratio below one tend to do?
quiz.explanation: Decrease the probability of disease. A positive likelihood ratio greater than one tends to increase probability, while a negative ratio below one tends to decrease it.
